 Ruddy, Forde and Bodvarsson: Wolves and Wrexham ‘played for both’ XI 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Ahead of Wolves’ Championship trip to Wrexham on Saturday, here is a combined XI of players from both clubs. ExpressAndStar.com highlights promotion winners and stalwarts from different eras.
 John Ruddy underpinned Wolves’ 2017/18 title, keeping 24 clean sheets and collecting the Golden Glove. He later served as back-up, left in 2022, then returned in 2026. He also had a loan spell at Wrexham in 2007.
 OneFootball Videos
 Aaron Hayden , a Wolves academy product, helped Wrexham win the 2022/23 National League and 2023/24 promotion, then rejoined Carlisle. Mickey Evans left Wolves without a senior game and became a Wrexham mainstay from 1966 to 1979, with promotions in 1969/70 and 1977/78. George Showell lifted the 1958 and 1959 titles and the 1960 FA Cup with Wolves before a spell at Wrexham.
 Ian Arkwright played four Wolves games, then delivered 104 league appearances and 10 goals for Wrexham. David Jones was key in Wolves’ 2008/09 promotion and later joined Wrexham, also contributing to the coaching staff.
 Darren Ferguson arrived from Manchester United, later winning promotion with Wrexham in 2002/03 and the 2005 Football League Trophy. Anthony Forde debuted for Wolves against Chelsea in 2011 and, as a wing-back, helped Wrexham to the 2022/23 National League title.
 Jon Dadi Bodvarsson, fresh from Euro 2016, scored on his Wolves debut and later had a brief Wrexham stint in 2024/25. Liam McAlinden featured in Wolves’ 2013/14 League One title and Wrexham’s 2022/23 success. Steven Fletcher hit 10 and 12 Premier League goals for Wolves, earned a reported £12million move to Sunderland, then scored 16 league goals while Wrexham climbed from League Two to the Championship.
